newsitem.title: UK: Standard falls as broker advises "sell".
newsitem.headline: Standard falls as broker advises "sell".

text.p: Shares in banking group Standard Chartered Plc fell on Wednesday as brokerage Collins Stewart changed its recommendation on the banking stock to a "sell" from a "hold", dealers said.
Standard shares fell 16p to 926-1/2p by 0748 GMT in an otherwise firm UK bank sector.
Market sources said SBC Warburg had also cut earnings forecasts for the banking group, though analyst Chris Ellerton at Warburg declined comment.
Mark Thomas, banking analyst at Collins Stewart, said he had cut his pre-tax profit forecast for the year end 1997 to 880 million stg from 920 million stg.
Thomas listed several factors for his negative stance, which included his projection that the level of bad debts may rise.
"It's not so much that the amount of bad debts will have increased, it is the level of recovery that is slower than anticipated," he said.

Thomas said tighter regulation by Hong Kong regulators on mortgage lending could reduce the growth of Standard's mortgage business in Hong Kong and sterling strength may have a negative impact on earnings.
The analyst also pointed out Standard could be vulnerable to any corporate tax changes in next months UK budget.
